fix_description: The symptom proves date-token expansion ran ("$YYYY/$MM/$hh/$mm/$ss" all expanded) yet skipped only "$DD" when it was immediately followed by 'T'. That expansion lives solely in GetDatedFileName (Helpers.cpp), which replaces each date token longest-first using negative lookaheads that were added/broadened during the recent metadata-token work (#41728/#44466) so date tokens like $D/$DD don't eat $DATE_TAKEN_/$DESCRIPTION/$DOCUMENT_ID. The day-token ($DD/$D) lookahead is over-broad and wrongly rejects a following 'T', leaving "$DD" literal. Fix: tighten the $DD/$D replacement regex so its lookahead only excludes genuine longer/metadata tokens (e.g. an extra 'D' for $DDD/$DDDD and the real metadata prefixes) rather than arbitrary trailing letters, restoring "$DDT" -> day+T, and add a HelpersTests.cpp regression case for "$DDT".
